answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a slowly earned, stake-backed reputation: each participant posts collateral, then earns trust only through repeated tasks whose outcomes are checked by independent peers. A whisper of praise alone cannot raise the score; the anchor is the peer-verified record, and penalties slash stake for proven fraud. A sybil attacker must fund every new identity and build its history over time, so splitting into many accounts multiplies locked capital and delays payoff. A terrace of cheap accounts gains no instant influence.
